newsitem.title: UK: British parliament Speaker steps into sleaze row.
newsitem.headline: British parliament Speaker steps into sleaze row.

text.p: The Speaker of Britain's parliament on Tuesday attacked media reports of sleaze among legislators, saying allegations against individual members were being used to suggest the whole political system was rotten.
Betty Boothroyd told the lower House of Commons that newspaper and television stories could prejudice the outcome of parliament's own investigation into allegations of misconduct.

"They should not use individual allegations as the occasion for highly generalised and unsubstantiated comments against members of this House as a whole and against our parliamentary system," she said.

Boothroyd had been stirred into making her unusually forthright comments by a recent television programme in which Mohamed Al-Fayed, the Egyptian-born owner of Harrods department store, was interviewed.

Fayed has alleged that he regularly paid former minister Neil Hamilton and some other MPs to represent his interests in parliament, and on one occasion provided Hamilton with a free room at the plush Ritz Hotel in Paris, which he owns.
Parliament's newly-appointed Commissioner for Standards, Sir Gordon Downey, and its Standards and Privileges Committee have started investigating aspects of the affair.

Last week Labour MP Tam Dalyell, claiming that the independent television programme had tarnished the good name of the Commons as a whole, appealed to Boothroyd to study a video of it and make her views known.

In her reply on Tuesday, Boothroyd said it was "deplorable" that many sections of the media drew only scant attention to the recent tightening-up by parliament of its procedures for investigation alleged malpractice.
She said the media had a valid role in bringing attention to the rare instances where MPs apparently breached parliamentary norms of honesty and probity.

"But it is reasonable to expect that the media do not repeat and pursue allegations in a way that prejudges their validity pending the outcome of investigations by the Parliamentary Commissioner for Standards," she added.
